purpose: Refresh measurements of the maintained public graph and distinguish current counts from retained historical interpretations.
publication_contract: The checked-in public-data baseline retains its dated historical observation report for the release replay. The final Makefile overlay computes the current report and public projections after historical validation. Read the measured-on field and method note in the deployed report; a historical baseline is not a current observation refresh.

method.canonical_public_entries: Nodes with public_visibility=public whose id is not redirected by canonical_redirects, using the same rule as the readable atlas.
method.developed_profiles: Distinct profile.node_id values resolving to those canonical public entries; publication_level=profile is counted separately.
method.literal_first_pass_entries: Canonical public nodes containing the exact lower-case substring 'first-pass entry' in the joined string values of the node record. This is a literal placeholder-wording count, not an assessment of every entry's quality. This legacy exact-phrase predicate misses biographical wording and must not be used as an overall completion measure.
method.first_pass_person_review_records: Canonical public person nodes whose review_status contains first_pass. This is a separate bibliographic status count.
method.graph_metrics: The existing apply_iteration_09.graph_metrics function resolves public endpoints and separates substantive relations from classification, evidence, documentary, and unresolved legacy lines. It does not deduce new relationships.
method.limits: Dataset counts do not establish source reading, intellectual importance, scholarly agreement, human acceptance, or completion of the registered research programmes.
method.biographical_first_pass_placeholder_desc: Canonical public person nodes whose description contains first followed by optional spaces, hyphens, or underscores and pass, case-insensitively. Counted separately from review status and profile presence.
method.unprofiled_first_pass_people: Canonical public people whose review_status contains first_pass and whose ID has no developed profile record.

observations.title: A readable entry and a developed profile are different records
observations.measurement: The current canonical public graph has {public_entries} entries and {developed_profiles} developed profile records ({profile_coverage_percent}%); {unprofiled_public_entries} canonical entries have no developed profile. Separately, {profile_label_entries} entries carry the publication-level label profile. Those labels do not create additional profile records.
observations.interpretation: An orientation, a publication label, and a developed account with sources are different units of work. Counting them together would overstate depth.
observations.implication: Choose a bounded set of entries, read the relevant sources, and develop specific accounts with locators and explicit uncertainty. Do not fill the gap with generic prose.
observations.test: Count canonical entries and actual profile records separately, then inspect the selected accounts and their source locators. A passing build is not editorial acceptance.

observations.title: Biographical placeholders remain unfinished
observations.kind: current literal-text measurement and scope explanation
observations.measurement: {biographical_first_pass_placeholder_descriptions} biographical descriptions still contain first-pass wording. {first_pass_person_review_records} person records retain first-pass status; {unprofiled_first_pass_people} of them have no developed profile. Separately, the legacy exact phrase first-pass entry occurs in {literal_first_pass_entries} canonical records. That exact-phrase count does not measure all unfinished first-pass content.
observations.interpretation: Publication-placeholder work does not establish biographical coverage. The biographical wording, review status, and actual profile records require separate checks.
observations.implication: Develop the unprofiled biographies from primary sources, explaining contributions, limits, and specific connections. Keep all public entries available for random exploration.
observations.test: Recompute each stated predicate and inspect the resulting IDs and profiles. Check that random selection reaches every canonical public entry; an exact-phrase count is not a completion test.

observations.title: Graph coverage does not establish agreement or source depth
observations.measurement: The canonical public projection has {typed_edges} typed relation rows, including {substantive_edges} substantive rows; {substantive_connected_nodes} entries have a substantive connection and {substantive_isolated_nodes} do not. The source register contains {sources} records, including {sources_with_public_links} with public links.
observations.interpretation: The measurement describes this atlas and the chosen relation filters. Source registration, an available link, a source reading, and an accepted claim are distinct.
observations.implication: Keep relation kinds, passage locators, review status, and rival interpretations visible. Refer to the dated research packets for what was actually read and to the unfinished-work register for what remains.
observations.test: Recompute the projection with the stated endpoint and relation rules. Trace an asserted connection to its source and locator; do not treat adjacency, a high degree, or a source count as proof.
